question_asked: I am a massive fan of well-done graffiti, and street art. Honestly, I believe it really gives cities character and an identity of their own. My hometown of Melbourne is famous for its colorful lane ways. Do you have much graffiti and street art in your town? How do you feel about it?
response: oh yea mate, street art is something i really dig too! we got heaps in the city, man. i typically encounter that on my jaunts around town, Hauz Khas village being a killer place for stunning artsy walls. quite a sight, it is. so cool, every time i walk by, feels like i'm part of a canvas. though, there are some who chose to turn it into a political platform, which is a bummer. but hey, can't control what everyone's gonna paint ya know? it still adds flavor to the place... reminds me, should post some pics on /r/streetart.

question_asked: Last weekend, I took a stroll on the Great Ocean Walk, in Victoria, Australia. It was serene, with the ocean waters hitting the rocks and the sun setting down in the backdrop. I loved it! Have you had any memorable hiking, or walking experiences in the vicinity of your location?
response: Oh for sure! We have the enchanting gorges over at Rouge, where I love to walk, especially when the leaves are changing. A stunning landscape opens up, with all the exquisite shades of fall, a splash of magic on the trees! And that's just one patch, there's so many gems here. Happy strolling to you though, that ocean walk sounds like a paradise!

question_asked: I'm a huge fan of street art and murals. Whenever friends are in town, I take them on a local graffiti tour that I made in Brooklyn. Does your city also have a creative arts scene that locals and tourists alike appreciate? What are some popular spots known for their artistic value?
response: Definitely! Love how cities use art to beautify and express their local culture. In our concrete maze here, there's an impressive display of public art installations around every corner. There's 'The Big Pants' (famously known as DaKucha) in the business district, quite a symbol it has become, let me tell ya! But for me, the real artistic soul of the place is in the hutongs. Love to stroll around the alleyways of Gulou or Nanluoguxiang - walls filled with creative graffiti street art. It's like a real-life Reddit thread, unpredictable and amusing! Keeps me rooted to my cultural roots but with a modern twist. So yea, if you're ever around this city, remember to explore beyond the towering skyscrapers, there’s a rich and vibrant world hiding in these narrow lanes!

question_asked: Last summer, I took a cooking class in Rome and absolutely fell in love with authentic Italian cuisine. One of my favorites dishes to prepare now is 'pasta alla carbonara'. But, I must admit, no matter how hard I try, it never tastes quite the same as it did in Rome. I guess it must have something to do with the local ingredients they use. What's a local dish from your area that you think I should try cooking?
response:
Oh la la, sounds like you've had a taste of the real deal in Rome! Here in Toronto (and by extension all of Canada), we're quite famous for Poutine. It's a dish with french fries topped with cheese curds and smothered in gravy. Sounds a bit strange eh, but trust me, you haven't lived till you've tried a solid poutine! You should absolutely give it a whirl, and it's relatively easy to make at home. Bonus points if you can get your hands on real cheese curds.
 
But personally, as a psycholgist I do find myself constantly analyzing why people are such fans of it- could it be the comfort-food-like warmth or the goofy blend of ingredients? Either way, it certainly keeps this gal happy as a beaver in the winter! Lol. Now my fellow Canadians, don't get all flapped at me, I know there are regional squabbles about the "correct' way to make it, but we can at least all agree it's a Canadian staple, right? :)

question_asked: I'm a huge football fan! I remember how the entire city of Liverpool erupted when the Reds won the Premier League in 2020 after a 30 year wait. It felt absolutely surreal! If you're into football, which club do you root for and why?
response: well ain't nothin' like gridiron football now, is it? Been tailgatin' all my life, even met my sweetheart in one o' them tailgate parties, ha! Funny thing is, back in our dating days we were on old school flip phones, wasn't no IG or TikTok to document those day - while sometimes heart dreams up a wild river walk tailgate party, hashtagging #TailgateLife and all, haha. As to my team, well, I've been loyal to my boys in silver and black, ever since they were the cardiac crew and till now as the Raider Nation. Catch the wave, y'all!

question_asked: One of my best mates recently moved from London to a small coastal town and he told me how he appreciates quiet beaches, seagulls, and mild weather. It sounds beautiful but I'm not sure I could ever swap my huge city life for a small coastal one. You know the hustle and bustle, iconic buildings, 24/7 business, and multicultural environment, I find thrill in it. But I was wondering, how would you describe the surroundings where you live? Is it more like a busy city or a calm town? Any iconic or distinct features?
response: Ah, that's an easy one mate! Picture yourself walking down cobblestone streets filled with mouthwatering aromas of fresh pasta, pizza, and roasted coffee wafting from every corner. You can feel the pulse of the city under your feet, buzzing with energy, rhythm, and life. A glance upward and you see weathered terracotta roofs juxtaposed against a backdrop of a modern cityscape. And, oh, the sounds! A cacophony of accents in the air, a testament of the rich cultural melting pot that I reside in. At the heart of it? Well, you've probably guessed it, an ancient amphitheatre standing strong & proud, whispering tales of gladiators and emperors. Bustling with so much action, it might as well stay awake all day, all night. But it isn't all city, there's a balance. Nature is close, just a short jaunt, and you suddenly find yourself surrounded by rolling vineyards which will make you forget about the city grip. So, city-but-not-too-much is the life for me. But hey, nothing against your friend's slow-paced beach life, we all find our peace somewhere. Whaddya think, would ya fancy a visit here pal?

question_asked: I have such fond memories of visiting local coffee shops in Belgium. There's something special about sipping a warm latte in a cozy café while observing the hustle and bustle of the city. I've always found the atmosphere of such places comforting. How do you feel about local cafes where you live? Do you have a favorite place to get coffee or tea? What's it like?
response: ah, lad, those little european cafes have a vibe of their own, don't they? now i might not be sipping coffee next to the grand palace, but i found this little place in kallio district i kinda like. it's like the grungy heart of the city with all it's street art and dive bars. cafe is chill, lots of students and artists hanging out, feels real cozy. plus they make a bang-on korvapuusti, quite a treat with a brew, no doubt. hasn't got the old world charm, but has a certain nordic charm to it for sure, haha.

question_asked: My experience with seafood in Maine was nothing short of phenomenal. Freshest lobsters I've ever had! Do you also have any seafood delicacies that your area is particularly proud of?
response: Absolutely mate, the seafood chowder here could give those lobsters in Maine a run for their money! Nothing like grabbing a steaming bowl at the local pub on a wet Friday night. Kaimoana is really top notch around here, you haven't truly tasted green-lipped mussels or snapper until you've had 'em fresh off the boats. Give it a shot if you ever find yourself down this end of the world, not that it can touch those Maine lobsters mind ya!

question_asked: I just got back from a road trip through some hot and dry states in the U.S., it felt like I was cooking inside my car! I visited Phoenix, and couldn’t handle the summer heat there. You really need a good air conditioner to live in those parts. I wonder, how's the weather during summer where you live? Is it hot there as well?
response: oh hombre, don't get me started on summers in Mexico city, porque they are hot, but nothing like Phoenix, nada that extreme. But si, a good AC is not really a luxury pero a necessity here. More than the heat tho, you have to deal with the humidity. Imagine being all drenchy and sticky, no me gusta nada. On the bright side tho, the nights can be cool and pleasant y la vista with all the city lights, worth it! But yeah, i completely get you, the heat can be unforgiving in some places, espero que sobreviviste el calor de Phoenix haha.

question_asked: My favorite holiday tradition is going ice fishing on the frozen lakes in northern Minnesota. The silence of snow carpeted landscapes is so soothing. Plus reeling in a big one out of an 8-inch hole in the ice is a lot of fun! Does your hometown have any unique winter traditions? How do you celebrate the winter season?
response: Pulling out the poncho and girding up for Ciclovia is a tradition here in my city. Our streets get splendidly quiet on car-free days, amigo. Even though nuestros inviernos aren't white snow and ice fishing kinda chill, they do bring a delightful cold! It's perfect for a bike ride, es muy relajante, i gotta tell ya. But, maybe I'll swap it out for a fishing rod one of these days, who knows, might be fun!

question_asked: I absolutely love visiting those glorious winter markets during the holiday season. Last year, I had the pleasure of hopping around several Christmas markets in different parts of Germany. It was a magical experience, especially the one in Dresden, where they make the largest Stollen! Have you ever had the experience of visiting a local holiday market, what kind of foods and traditions do you usually find there? What's your favorite bit about it?
response: oh mate, you’ve hit the nail there. being part of a tropical nation, our holiday markets aren't all about mulled wine or roasting chestnuts like i'm guessing its in Germany, but they're an experience nevertheless! Tons of local food stalls pop up selling dishes from every corner of our country. You haven’t experienced real holiday market fun till you’ve tried ’munkoyo’ - our own traditional non-alcoholic beverage. Gives you a bit of a vino vibe but also has a unique fermented edge. And who can forget tasty ‘Nshima’! Also, we've a thing called 'unity dance', it's like our Christmas jig, haha. Favourite bit? A tie between the foods and dancing. Its that moment where the hustle of the city seems to pause, and all that’s left is good cheer and belly-ache laughs. Perfect time to unwind after pounding those wards floors, right?  Interesting hearing about the largest stollen...so the holiday market is just like reddit, always something surprising!

question_asked: I've just come back from a week-long trip exploring breweries in Belgium. It was fantastic! Belgian beers are something special, right! The trappist beers from Chimay, Rochefort, and Westvleteren are some of my favorites. Do you have a favorite foreign beer, and why is it your favorite? Is it easily available where you live?
response: Surely, Belgian beers are something else! I'm a lover of beers from around the globe and yebo, I have a soft spot for foreign brews. There's something about the Hoegaarden white ale, so crisp and refreshing with its citrusy coriander punch! Just sublime, I tell ya. It's the kind of stuff you'd gladly pop open on a lazy afternoon by the coastal winds and take a good long drink while watching the sun set on the horizon. Our bottle stores carry it, so it's not a mission to find. Lucky me, right? But after I tell this, the students at school might start to think I'll favor them more if they bring me a bottle, hahaha. A principal's dilemma, isn't it?

question_asked: As someone who used to live in quite a small town, I loved the feel of community there, every corner was a familiar face. And not to mention the "famous" bakery in town, their apple pie was to die for. Now I live in a bustling city which has skyscrapers all around. What is your favorite type of location - the silent tranquility of a small town, or the bustling hustle of a city? Do you have a favorite shop or restaurant which is unique to your local community?
response: Hmm. for me, each has their charm, ya know? Growing up, I've got hazy memories of the familiar cluman's bakery in my old place, god those scones! But now, working through 18 hour shifts, the city's constant buzz is kinda comforting... keeps me from dozing off ya know... Hehe! Not to mention the constant chatter of my fellow online Zambians during every odd hour. But what really has my heart is this hole-in-the-wall shop near the clinic that sells these bomb chicken pies, seriously, to die for. Can't get stuff like that back in my old small town, no siree!

question_asked: I grew up in the shadows of the Rocky Mountains in Colorado, and the variety of nature and wildlife there was astounding. I loved hiking and exploring, especially trying to spot the state bird, the Lark Bunting, or other elusive creatures. I'm curious, what kind of wildlife do you encounter in your neck of the woods? You ever stumble across any particularly interesting critters while out for a walk or hike?
response: Oh, no mountain ranges for me, mate! My treks generally involve a sea breeze brushing past me and tons of birds (cockatoos can get noisy, I tell you!). Once I did stumble upon a band of eerie fruit bats in a park during an evening stroll. Not exactly Rocky Mountains material, but an adventure in its own right! Love observing the diverse wildlife, just as much as I love nosediving into internet rabbit holes.

question_asked: I always enjoyed strolling through farmers markets. Last time I visited the Pike Place Market in Seattle, it was such a vibrant experience. The aroma of fresh seafood, flowers, and brewed coffee was awesome! Do you ever visit farmers markets in your town? What's your favorite thing to buy?
response: Oh la la, farmers markets are the essence of life! I currently live in Paris and we have these quaint little markets pretty much everywhere. Last Sunday, I visited the one at Rue Poncelet, and man, can't tell you how lively it was - almost like a festival! Those glossy red tomatoes, ripened camemberts and the assortment of olives...C'est la vie! My heart always nudges towards the art postcards - I am an art curator after all, cher ami! It’s a habit I have, buying those postcards - a simple souvenir which is essentially a small piece of art for me, mon dieu! p.s – if you felt a waft of nostalgia smelling that brewed coffee, wait till you smell the freshly baked croissants here, heaven!

question_asked: I love going to the farmer's market here in Seattle, the freshness of the produce and the variety is just amazing. There's a sense of community that I really appreciate. I've noticed that every region has it's own unique produce and specialties. What are some fresh produce or local specialties that you can find in your farmer's market?
response: oh hey there! the farmers markets down here in San Antonio are quite the scene. you can't swing a stick without hitting some amazing local honey or salsa. we actually have a lil' gem called the Pearl Farmers Market - love the hustle and bustle there. they got plenty of farm-fresh eggs, meat, and artisan bread. one of my favs is the local poteet strawberries, those are straight-up addictive, and don't get me started on the Texas peaches in season, a whole different ball game! my personal trick tho, after a heavy day at the shop, i whip up a quick dinner with all the fresh goodies i scored and relax with a nice glass of Texas wine. You see, we're not just all about the Alamo and cowboy hats here in SA, haha!

question_asked: I've been living in the heart of Britain for quite some time now and one thing that truly amuses me is the punk fashion scene right in the Camden Market. It's still kicking it, post all these years! I believe every location has a unique fashion style or a specific local market that's popular. What's that exclusive style statement or popular local market in your area?
response: Ah, right in the middle of "denden town", you've got loads of geeks sporting everything from the nerdiest video game tees to full-blown anime cosplays. And man, electronics market around here? It's on a whole different level. It's basically the "Silicon Valley" of Japan, haha. Still, It's not all about digital, we got our unique charm you know, it's like walking around in an anime of it's own. Shame we ain't hitting global fame like that infamous fish market in the capital though.

question_asked: Last month, I had the chance to visit Quebec City in Canada and it was a beautiful place full of history. The weather was very chilly, but the Quebecois don't seem to let that bother them at all. They headed out to ice skate and enjoyed the snow in their colorful outfits. How do people in your city usually spend their winter weekends?
response: oh man, winters here give a new meaning to chilling inside. my personal fave is grabbing my laptop, burrowing under a cozy blanket & surfing reddit with a piping hot mug of glühwein...yup, the real deal, not the stuff from the supermarket. but yeah, like in Quebec, peeps here don't particularly hibernate just cause it's cold. they be out there on the frozen lakes, doing some crazy ice kitesurfing. admittedly, it looks fun, might just take it up one of these days... you know, after I've done my daily reddit ration of course. gotta have priorities, right? 😅👩‍💻🍷⛸️

question_asked: I absolutely love the local delicacies at the Strasse market here in Berlin. Don't even get me started on the currywurst and the variety of local cheeses, it's pure heaven! Talking about food experiences, have you got a favorite local dish in your city? Any particular street food tradition that you can't live without? Or maybe something that you think is unique to your place?
response: Ah mate, your taste buds are having a fest there with that currywurst! Buenos Aires, where I'm puttin' my life together right now, is pretty much a carnivore's heaven haha! Parrillada is what we're crazy about here. This barbecued variety of meat cuts, offal, sausages is absolute love. I'd say the fernet con coca is something unique we have here, it's our go-to drink that's kind of an acquired taste. And don't get me started on Empanadas, probably the most popular street food here. Man, if you're ever down here, hit me up, we'll have an Argentinian feast!

question_asked: I recently moved to this big, glowing city of lights - New York. It's crazy up here, the rush, the hustle and all the skyscrapers. What a view at night! But, sometimes I really miss my home town's open fields and that beautiful smell of lavender. You see, I come from this small town in France with acres of lavender fields. The picturesque sight and the calming smell is truly unique, makes you want to lose yourself in the magnificence of nature, you know? Do you have some unique natural feature in your hometown or city that makes it stand out?
response: Jassis, here in Cape Town, we're absolutely spoiled by Mother Nature, I tell you! I mean, we've got Table Mountain right here, practically on our doorstep, and it's seriously one of the most beautiful sights you'll ever see. Almost everywhere you look in the city, there it is...as if watching over us all the time. And the smell of fynbos on a hike up there, it's intoxicating, something truly unique to this part of South Africa. And don't even get me started on our beaches, hey. They're just as wonderful, but in a different, more sort of a refreshing way. So, yeah, I reckon if you've got a thing for nature, you best come visit Cape Town my friend, it's a kaleidoscope of natural beauty. But hey, I wouldn't mind losing myself for a while in your French lavender fields, sounds like a dream!

question_asked: I recently started a small herb garden on my balcony in Seattle. It's such a relaxing hobby, and the herbs smell absolutely fantastic. I got basil, cilantro, and mint so far. How about you? Are you into any kind of plants or gardening? What's growing well in your climate?
response: Ah, the ol' green thumb. Nice one, mate! Been toying with the idea myself, tried growing a bit of wasabi on the side in my apartment's balcony (you know, the stuff you get with your sushi... delicious). Wasabi is surprisingly tricky though, bit of a diva really. But apart from that, got some shiso and mitsuba for the occasional home-made miso soup. Right now, kind of leaning towards trying out ichimi togarashi (Japanese chili pepper). Might add a bit of 'kick' to my ramen. Here's hoping mine ends up being as fragrant as your herbs!

question_asked: I love grabbing a coffee from my favorite French cafe here in New Orleans. The ambiance just feels right and brings the spirit of Paris right into Louisiana. I'm curious, do you have a coffee shop or cozy cafe that you visit often? What's it like over there?
response: totally! there's this spot i frequent that harks to the traditional fika cafes folks love round here. tucked away off the main streets, it's quaint but modern in design; guess that's my inner architect appreciating it. let's just say, their cardamom buns are to die for and the aroma of fresh coffee makes a fantastic start to my day. oh, and another thing, it's a real gathering spot, buzzing with digital nomads and old friends catching up. always a mix of convos in the air, feels really, idk, communal?

question_asked: Back in my university days, I was part of the rowing team. Nothing quite like the feeling of gliding over the cool water at the crack of dawn with your crew, feeling like you're part of something bigger. We used to travel all across the country for championships and regattas, from the busy Charles River in Boston to the serene Potomac in Washington D.C. Do you have any rowing clubs nearby where you live? Or any other spots where people usually go to for recreational activities?
response: Rowing, huh? I can completely get the allure, especially at dawn when the world's just stirring awake. I haven't rowed myself, though I've dreamed about giving it a shot. In my corner of the world, kayaking's a bit more of the go to. There's this specific spot, right out to the Atlantic, that the locals swear by. Get quite territorial about it too, heh, it's kinda adorable. I prefer my morning jog by the riverside here in Bairro Alto - what can I say? Some solid ground under my feet is more my speed, and the view of the April 25th Bridge is totally worth it.

question_asked: Oh, I'm such a sucker for visiting historic sites and learning about the local history and culture. Just last summer I visited the Colosseum in Rome and it was simply breathtaking. The blend of history and culture truly makes a visit to such a place an enriching experience. Do you have any historic landmarks in your city that you love to visit, or you feel they represent your city's history and culture?
response: oh absolutely! love little historical gems in our own backyards, don't we? have you heard of something known as 'Fika'? it's basically a culture treasured by swedes where we take out time to enjoy coffee n some sweet treats with friends or even solo. needless to say, architecture, being all about art n history, is closely woven into this whole 'Fika' culture too. Have you ever been to a 'Fika' session in a building dating back to the 1700s? I have, and boy, these gorgeous structures stand testimony to the passage of time and culture. trust me, that's a different level of 'Fika' my friend. makes me feel like i'm sipping coffee right in the heart of swedish history!редел

question_asked: Last Sunday, I decided to get out of the house and head to the local farmers market here in San Francisco. I felt so spoilt for choice with all the fresh, local produce — especially the artisan cheeses and sourdough bread; I mean, look, there's nothing quite like the smell of fresh-baked bread in the morning! How's the fresh produce where you live? Any special local delicacies or regional specialties you enjoy?
response: Ah mate! Lemme tell ya, there's this huoguo place a few sois over from the Nest..immense! All sorts of fresh veggies n meats boiling in this flavorful broth, it's a must try. And don't get me started on the night market with those steaming soup dumplings, delicacy of my part of the world for a reason. Can taste them anytime, anywhere. Now, if only local treats could compensate for the un-bloody-believable commuting woes in this godforsaken concrete jungle lol. Gotta hunt high n low for those local gems, but that's where the fun lies, innit?

question_asked: As a huge sports fan, I've been to a bunch of different stadiums around the world. It's always a different vibe, right? Last time I visited the Wembley Stadium in London, it was buzzing! I wonder, have you been to any big sports events recently? How was the atmosphere?
response: Not a huge sports person myself, more of the Reddit-browsing-in-a-cosy-corner type to be honest. I do mosey down to the stadium when the All Blacks are playing a match though. The atmosphere is bonkers mate! Whole place buzzes with energy, even though your bones freeze in the open stands. You've got half the country belting out the Haka, faces painted, screaming their lungs out. Summat else, I tell ya! Makes you feel right a part of something big, don't it? That's Kiwi spirit for you.

question_asked: I have a crazy love for Football, in my country Spain, it is a huge part of everyone's life. Everyone here has a favorite club and it's almost like a tradition. What's your take on Football? Is there a local club in your city that you cheer for? If so, I'd love to hear about their achievements or famous matches.
response: Ah mate, football's my jam! Grew up playing it on the streets back home, brought the love here too. Arsenal FC, man. The Gunners! Nothing beats a good night out down at the Emirates, minus emptying the old wallet of course. Cheers for the Invincibles – still on cloud nine from that '03-'04 season. Seems like ages ago... Well, lot's of ups and downs since then but loyalty stays strong, yeah? What can I say, the highs are worth the lows!

question_asked: I've always been a big fan of roller coasters. Just last summer, I had an unforgettable trip to Six Flags in New Jersey with some friends. We rode The Joker, El Toro, and the Bizarro roller coaster and had the time of our lives. How about you? Are there any amusement parks near you with some unforgettable rides?
response: ah mate, believe it or not, where i'm residing it's more about the culture and less about thrill rides haha. don't get me wrong, i'm not against a bit of adrenaline rush. there's this modest little spot in the shape of an Asterix not too far, got a few decent rides honestly. But man, would kill for a Six Flags experience some day, bet it trumps staring at paintings and sipping wine haha. Maybe once i've soaked in enough Monet, i shall.

question_asked: I can't help but think back to the time I did the scariest thing ever- bungee jumping from Macau Tower in China. The city view from the top was breathtaking. Do you have a similar adventure spot around you that is popular for extreme sports? Maybe a high bridge or a tower?
response: Mate, did the Macau Tower jump too. But locally I got my fill of the rush from a different beast, Gaelic games. A solid round of Hurling or a manic match of Gaelic football, I tell ya, your heart pounds harder than jumping off a tower! If you're here in the shadow of Guinness HQ, I reckon you should give em a try! For conventional thrills, there’s bungee jumping near the Liffey on occasion. But... it’s got nothing on the Macau Tower, lad.

question_asked: I recently got to visit the famous La Sagrada Familia in Barcelona. The intricate design and attention to detail in the architecture was simply amazing! Have you ever visited a similar kind of architectural masterpiece close to you? If so, could you tell me a bit about it?
response: ahh i've been near the spire, mate, and i tell you that thing's a right pointy needle to the sky. can't say it's got the complexities of la sagrada familia, more like a toothpick next to a carved roast hah! but highlight of my night out in town is always when i stumble out of the pub and see it scraping the dark sky. it's pretty lit at night too! as an added bonus, there's a chipper shop just round the corner for the post-pub munchies. Blarney chips have got nothin on 'em. fair enough, i suppose. a simple pointy structure for a simple single lad! not much for the complexitiy and grandiosity that life and architecture can offer, haha.

question_asked: I had a chance to pick up some locally grown habanero peppers from a farmer's market last weekend here in Mexico. I used them to spice up my salsa, and it was fire! How about you? Do you enjoy spicy food? What's the spiciest thing you've ever eaten from your local cuisine?
response: you know, I'm a real sucker for some heat in my food. reminds me of this little time in Hell's Kitchen (no, not the Gordon Ramsay show, lol), there’s a hole-in-the-wall Asian joint that sells these terrifyingly spicy dumplings. made me feel like a dragon breathing fire, no kidding. But, tbh, keeping it on the DL cause I can’t really afford to eat out that often. you know being a broke film student, part-timing it and all, haha. Ended up treating myself after landing a gig though. Damn, my mouth is watering just thinking about it now! Think I might juz have to save up for another round of fire dumplings from this local spot again soon!

question_asked: I've always been a huge fan of food, especially from different regions and cultures. Last week, I had a delicious bowl of pho in one of my local Vietnamese restaurants in San Francisco. I was wondering, what's your favorite local dish, and do you have any particular restaurant recommendation for it?
response: oh man, now you're speaking my language or rather, my stomach's haha. Talking about local delicacies, it's hard to escape the humble Ruisleipä topped with salmon. It's simple, but oh, so satisfying! There's a small joint close to where I work - the white-collar playground, where they do it just right with the freshest ingredients. I wield a scalpel for a living, so trust me when I tell you about clean cuts and fresh, haha! However, whenever the missus and I feel fancy, we trade our scrubs for dinner jackets and head over to the place with a sick view of the sea. The name of the place? Well, lets just say it rhymes with Favintola. A doctor's gotta keep some secrets, right mate? ;)

question_asked: I just love winter sports. Spending a season working at a ski resort was one of the best experiences of my life. We had visitors from all over the world who came to enjoy the beautiful snow of the Rocky Mountains in Colorado. Where do you head to for your winter sports fix? Have you ever tried skiing or snowboarding?
response: As a creature of warm weather, mate, the idea of voluntarily spending time in snow tends to give me the shivers, no pun intended. That being said, admittedly, Table Mountain does offer an awe-striking view and serene moments, particularly early in the morning. Rather than skiing or snowboarding, I'd probably choose a steep hike and then to reward myself with a hearty breakfast at the top! A hot cuppa in this weather against that backdrop, absolute bliss! Props to you for the energy, gotta appreciate the enthusiasm for sliding down icy hills, haha.

question_asked: I've been recently into gardening, taking care of plants has always been a relaxing hobby for me. Some of my plants are from my travels around the globe. Like my cacti, which I got from a trip to Phoenix, or tulip bulbs from Amsterdam. By the way, do you have a plant that is popular or native to your area?
response: oh yeh, I'm not much of a green thumb but gardening seems real nice and a cool way to remember travels. 🌵 here in Gothenburg, we've got quite a few cute lil public orchards and apple trees are everywhere! Seems like every lil park or patch of grass here has apple trees. Not by any means native to here, but defs a staple of the city. There are also a lot of birch trees native to Sweden, you can't throw a stone without hitting one here haha. Also, just FYI, Sweden is kinda known for its bilberries (sort of like a wild blueberry), which grows in the forests around the city during august-ish. have you tried any bilberry? They're pretty tasty! 🌳🍎🍏

question_asked: Ever since I visited Disneyland in Florida, I've had this obsession with theme parks. I just love the thrill of the rides and the creativity behind those magical places. Have you got a favorite theme park near your area and what's the best ride in your opinion?
response: oh, you're talking my kinda fun! Closest thing we got here for a good thrill is Ratanga Junction, with it's ol' Cobra, a roller-coaster that'll seriously mess up your hairdo lol. They shutdown for some time, but the memories of those upside-down moments still give me chills. If you ever found yourself down south, would recommend it. But I hear they've moved some of their rides to a new place now. Must check that out sometime...may just discover a new favourite!

question_asked: I recently started getting into gardening, I live in a small apartment in the city and have only a tiny balcony but I still managed to dedicate a corner to my little plants. It's crazy how fresh soil and leaf growth can make me feel so grounded, especially now with all the lockdowns. Do you have any green spaces near your home that you love to visit?
response: You've got the right idea! There's something profoundly satisfying about nurturing life, ain't it? Now and then I love being around the stunning Kirstenbosch Botanical Gardens. It's a striking greenspace hugged by Table Mountain that has a unique variety of plants indigenous to the region and it's just a joy to spend some time in on the weekends. Also, my local school's garden is my go-to zen space, working in education makes it quite convenient. Keep up your gardening! :)

question_asked: I've been recently focusing my attention on urban birds. It's amusing to see how they adapt to the big city's environment. Lately, I noticed more and more pigeons and sparrows in Chicago. Tell me, do you notice any change in the bird population in your area? Do you recognize some species?
response: Oh-la-la, didn't think I'd ever give this some thought until you brought it up, mate! What a curious point of view. Just recently realized I've been hearing fewer morning coos of those Parisian pigeons near my window. Always been more of a seagull girl myself - growing up in a coastal city does that to you! And these little guys, think they're nightingales? Start singing their tiny hearts out as soon as the sun sets. Bit of a rollercoaster soundscape around here, lol!

question_asked: Growing up in Canada, I always made sure to see the Northern Lights, or Aurora Borealis, at least once a year. Such a magical sight never fails to mesmerize me. What's the signature natural phenomenon where you live that people would generally not want to miss?
response: Oh mate, let me tell you, where I'm from, I often crave a bit of the Canucks cold! Here we're more about sweat than snow. Spent my childhood staring up at the Andes, not quite as shimmery as your Northern Lights but majestic mountains they are, I tell ya. The real spectacle is down south though, blue giants of ice that'll make you feel like an ant. To answer your question, those sights are even more scarce on reddit than at home! Cheers from the land of Malbec.

question_asked: Going out on weekends is something I really enjoy. Whether it is going to watch a football match or just visiting a local pub around the corner, it's always great fun! Although getting to Emirates Stadium requires me to take a long underground journey, I still wouldn't trade that experience for anything else. How about you? Are there any interesting sports events or places near where you live?
response: Ah, hitting the local watering hole and enjoying matches definitely paints a cozy picture, eh! Although, more than pubs and lagers, what really gets me going are those beautiful Swedish pines. I enjoy a bracing walk around the Holmenkollbakken - one of the world's oldest ski jumps, when the snow's all crunchy, perfect to strap on the planks! Can't deny the charm of building a snowman later on with the grandkids, then warming up my bones with a hot toddy in the cabin. Not your traditional sports event, but it's quite the Viking way, ain't it!

question_asked: I've been learning to prepare sushi lately and it's quite an art, I should say. Of course, I can't compare my skills with any sushi masters. Here in Los Angeles, there's such a variety of global cuisine that it's great to explore and try to replicate some at home. Have you experienced any exotic cuisine that you've really enjoyed and have tried to cook at home? Maybe there's a local dish that you're an expert at cooking?
response: Ah, sushi, my friends from the west seem to love it, it has such an delicate art and chemistry to it, tones of small things to get just right to recreate the flavor. Been into it a bit myself, but I tell you bud, where I am from, food tends to be a little bit spicier, more robust flavors. Now i usually enjoy my spicy paneer after a long day at the...library. Getting the spicy gravy right is finicky business, but when you do, oh boy, levels of masalas, heat and aromatics just transcend any ordinary food experience, haha. Oh, and did i tell you about 'puchka', the king of street foods from, ahem, my childhood town! Geez, I’d kill for a good puchka stand in this hot bustling city, I tell ya!

question_asked: I always find it interesting to see how different regions treat various sporting events. Like here in the Northwest of the US, we are all crazy about football, especially on Super Bowl day. What sport gets your folks riled up in your area on a big match day?
response: Ah, I can tell our locals aren't as football-obsessed as you guys in the northwest of the states. Our city, often confused with the fashion capital yeah, it's annoying, but I mean it's understandable, considering how closely they resemble each other in namesake, and of course, class, has quite the sturdy affinity for "le beau jeu". You can bet that when the national team plays, especially during summer tournaments, the excitement is off the charts! Chatting amongst fellow 'art appreciators' online, oh those threads can become battlegrounds quicker than a Royce flick and trick, haha. This fervor is matched, no, maybe even surpassed by our local club games, particularly the bitter "Classique". Football is indeed the city's heartbeat.

question_asked: As a foodie, one of my favorite pastimes is exploring and trying out local delicacies. There's this dish I fell in love within Shizuoka, Japan: "Sakuraebi no Tempura", a crispy, tempura-fried cherry shrimp that can only be fished from Suruga Bay. I'm curious if you have a local dish that you love and is unique to your place?
response: oh man, you're getting me started on food! here, you can't beat the monjayaki, a tokyo special. it's this gooey delight that has everything from cabbage to seafood thrown in, fried right on the hotplate. You get to practice some sweet okonomiyaki-making skills but the taste is totally different thou. And when it's cold like it is now, there's nothing more comforting than digging into some oden at an old street stand in Shinjuku! Seriously this is some food paradise in my area, making my programming-bod regret every meal haha. You should try it the next time you're passing through, totally the food haven without the Kansai/Kanto bragging y'know?

question_asked: I absolutely love hiking. There's something about being one with nature that's truly magical. One of the finest hiking trails I've gone through was in the Appalachian range. It was actually quite tough but so worth the effort. What about you? Do you also enjoy hiking? And what's your opinion on the most challenging or rewarding hiking spots in or around your area?
response:
Mate, being an astronomer and all, I can tell ye I've spent hundreds, if not thousands, of nights under the stars. But hiking? I'd need a wee bit more physics for that, haha! 

And here in Edinburgh, you're never too far from a cheeky hill to climb. Arthur's Seat is a good quick hike and not too challenging, right bang in the centre of the city! You can see all the way to glasgow from the top on a clear day. Mind, it can get very nippy up there, this being Scotland and all. 

The Pentland Hills though, now there's a proper hike. It gets quite rugged in places, especially on a dreich day. But the views on a bright day, now that's a reward in itself, and a perfect place to set up the telescope on a clear night, the sight of the Milky Way really makes it worth your while. So there ye go mate, as we say here in  Scotland: "There's no such thing as bad weather, only the wrong clothes"!

question_asked: I am so fascinated by the world's landscapes, seriously. Last summer, I took a trip to Banff in Canada and the glimmering turquoise waters of Moraine Lake quite literally took my breath away! What's the most picturesque place you've been to near where you live? Or perhaps a place your friends often go to for some great clicks?
response: Ah, the landscapes you describe sound surreal, mate. Your experience reminds me of a place near home here in Rome, called "Civita di Bagnoregio". It's just a couple of hours away and lemme tell ya, it's magnificent. It's an ancient hill town hanging onto its existence atop a plateau in the Italian countryside. With a hollowed out network of caves and tunnels beneath the buildings and the only access being a pedestrian bridge, it sure is something outta a fairy tale. Gets a lot of the insta crowd too, always posing with the town in the background, hehe. Kinda makes for an interesting contrast between the ancient-ness of the place and the modern-ness of social media ya know...being a chef I have a keener eye for food than landscapes, but I gotta admit, Civita di Bagnoregio, is dang pretty.

question_asked: I recently had a breathtaking trip to the Grand Canyon, Arizona. The landscape was staggeringly beautiful and the journey was a blast. This got me thinking, if you had to pick a place where you live, which natural wonder or place of interest would you suggest I should visit next and why?
response: oh man, the Grand Canyon sounds like a proper blast, super jel here. Gotta say, we've got some lovely spots for a wander back at my end too. In the heart of the city, right where things tend to get a bit too chaotic, there's this dreamy canal ring, perfect for a bike ride or a casual stroll. nothing like the wide open space of the canyon, but, adds its own twist of historic buildings and ridiculously pretty bridges. Few wee hours into the day, the orange glow on em is what dreams made of, mate! But if you're more of the lets-get-lost-in-nature type, the sand dunes up north will literally blow ya away, pun intended. The old windmill out there adds a heck of charm. Not the Grand Canyon, but it’s got that Dutch charisma, ya get me?

question_asked: I've always been fascinated by unique landscapes. Back when I lived in Albuquerque, New Mexico, I would take long hikes along the Sandia Mountains to enjoy the picturesque views. It was surreal in the spring when the wildflowers were out and about. If you were to take a leisurely stroll or hike, how would you describe the local landscapes you'd encounter and walk by?
response: Well mate, on this side of the Mediterranean, we got some pretty unique landscapes as well. El Retiro Park is one of the loveliest green patches in the urban hustle, full of age-old trees and grand statues from a time long past. It's always calming walking by the calm lake, its mirror-like surface a reflection of the world around. Paseo de la Castellana is quite a sight with its bustling lively lanes and grand architecture, making one think about Spain's rich historical canvas. If you want more rugged though, we are just a short drive away from epic mountain scenes, like in Sierra de Guadarrama. I do love my weekend hikes around there if I manage to break away from the chaos of the city. All in all, there is plenty to see and explore! Aye, different from your Sandia Mountains, but breathtaking nonetheless.

question_asked: I remember when I was a kid, my family would take me to this super-famous amusement park every summer. Ah, the sweet and cotton-candy memories those days were. To this day, I am a roller-coaster junkie, and try to go to as many theme parks as possible. Do you have an amusement park near where you live? Which ones have you been to and how did you find the rides?
response:
Ah the nostalgia of childhood trips to amusement parks, mate! Around here I've got the old guy Efteling, a classic, right? Some say it's for kids, but don't let the fairy tales fool ya. It’s a solid day of adventure, even for us grown-ups, with that crazy Baron 1898 mine drop. Phew! Serious pucker factor, man! Who knew been dropped down a supposed haunted mine shaft could be that thrilling?!

But the real gem, literally a crazy 15min-quick hop from my rent-limited rooftop view, is Walibi Holland. Oh man, the Goliath ride is not for weak hearts or stomachs. I’ve lost count on how many times I might've left my stomach in mid-air while having a go at it, haha! I’d rate that dude as one of the top-notch in coaster madness for sure.

Got any crazy good coaster stories of your own, buddy? Share the amusement park thrills!

question_asked: I'm such a foodie, and I love trying out different kinds of food from all around the world. Just last week, I had some amazing shepherd's pie and black pudding at this quaint little English pub in my city. Do you have a favorite local dish or food that you'd absolutely recommend to someone visiting your city?
response: Bringing gastronomy to the table, headlines are typically stolen by Tacos Al Pastor, but I'm gonna share what I consider a real gem: Tostadas de Atún from Contramar. It’s like a flavor fiesta in your mouth, you get the kick of freshly caught tuna, a little bit of heat from chipotle mayonnaise, and to top it off cripsy leek. Pair it with a cold michelada for a godly combo. English pub food sounds hearty tho, shepherd’s pie and black puds ain't something you come across every streetside.

question_asked: I've always had a fascination with skyscrapers. During my trip to Dubai, I was simply mesmerized by the colossal structures and the architectural wonders like Burj Khalifa. What about you? Do you have any interesting and iconic landmarks or architectural marvels near where you live?
response: we've got a bucket here, ahem, the bucket fountain to be precise. It's a neat quirky landmark, not exactly like a sky-kissing tower, more like an unpredictable, whimsical, sort of oddball sculpture. it's not your typical architectural marvel, but it's got a charm of its own. love watching the buckets tip over, sometimes it's like they got a life of their own! On the plus side, no risk of acrophobia! ;)

question_asked: I had a fantastic time last year when I got to visit Japan and explored some of their most famous shrines. One of the highlights was the Fushimi Inari Shrine in Kyoto, which is famous for its thousands of vermilion torii gates. Now, I am curious. Have you visited any historical landmarks or significant places in your area? Can you share some of their names or a bit of their story?
response: oh man, I wish I could travel to those cool places myself soon eh, nothing beats the serenity of those shrines. here, it's a bit different. We've got some history embedded in our streets. Monserrate is one place that comes into mind, feels like a pilgrimage every time I climb that hill! Then there's the Museo del Oro, homing gold artifacts. Quite entrancing when you realize how much our ancestors valued gold and the stories associated with it. Then there's La Candelaria, a colorful neighborhood with preserved colonial architecture. There's always a story to find in each corner around here, takes me back centuries every time I stroll through. I'd say my city's quite the historical hotspot too! Felt like time-traveling while telling you all about it lol.

question_asked: I've been pretty obsessed with football (or soccer, as some like to call it) over the years. Being a fan of Liverpool FC, the energy at Anfield is out of this world. How about you, my friend? Do you have a local football team you cheer for? How is their performance usually in their league?
response: Oh, mate, if only our lads could match that ferocious Anfield energy! I back the Serie A team close to my heart, the boys with wolf and twins as the symbol. It ain't been their prime days lately tho, pal. Oh, to re-live the time when Totti and De Rossi used to grace the field! As it stands, we're a long way from the top, not to mention those folks from the club symbolic of black and white stripes who often roll the winning wheel. But what is football without its highs, lows, and occasional ref-bashing, eh? You ready for the upcoming season? Let's hope our teams deliver some dazzling goals, eh?

question_asked: I was perfectly happy to stay inside during the lockdown, having never been much of an outdoor person anyway. But I did miss all the street food you can get here in Thailand. Have you ever missed anything due to the lockdowns where you are?
response: Oh ja, as a Norwegian who pretty much lives online, lockdown wasn't too bad for me either. I was missing outdoor activities though. Not because they're my thing, but here in Oslo, we have this tradition of 'tur' or as you guys would say, 'hiking.' Just put on some decent boots, packed lunch and we head out to explore the forest or mountains.. it's a pretty nice way to spend a weekend. But with all the restrictive measures last year, mista my chance to complain about how tur is not my cup of tea while secretly enjoying those sweet moments of solitude in nature. Ended up spending most of them arguing with people on reddit, haha. It didn't necessarily fill the void, but it helped to keep my mind off things.

question_asked: I was out stargazing last night, one of my favorite pastime hobbies. There is something fascinating about gazing at the celestial bodies up there. One thing that always strikes me is how different the night sky appears depending on where you are. During my last trip to Alaska, it was the Northern Lights that stole the show! Do you also enjoy stargazing? How does the sky usually look on a clear night where you are?
response: Night sky view here in the city? mate, pretty dim due to the light pollution. Seriously, Tokyo Game Show glow is nothing compared to all the neon lighting us all the time. But ye, still can catch few of the bright fellas. Orion, ready to slay on winter nights, Big Dipper pointing its celestial way. Hiking Mount Fuji, now, that's a different story, stars blanketing you, Milky Way looking like a divine bridge. Aye, there's something humbling about that experience, puts things in perspective.

question_asked: I'm a total foodie and love trying out different delicacies. One of my favorite gastronomic adventures was when I visited Japan and tried the real deal - sushi! So tell me, do you have a favorite local cuisine that's peculiar to where you live?
response: aha, you've struck a chord with a fellow foodie! The nip in the air has got me yearning for one true love, karjalanpiirakka _ yes, yes, supposed to be a dessert, but who's telling, right? 😉 And a must with that my friend, is egg butter! cornucopia of simple yet bang on flavors. Slap on that salty goodness and you'll be in a world you'd never want to return from. Now I'm making myself drool on the keyboard, oh man! Baked till golden, got this crispy crust and this creamy rice pudding interior... Man oh man! 🤩 Perfect bite amidst the hustle and bustle of surgeries, keeps me humming - though I suppose that's a good thing, hahaha.

question_asked: I just got back from a road trip, which was absolutely amazing.  We drove through all sorts of diverse landscapes - the dense forests of Oregon, the stunning coastlines in California, and the breathtaking deserts in Nevada. The radio kept me company, introducing me to local bands and music scenes I would've never found otherwise. Do you have any favorite radio stations or local bands where you live?
response: Road trips, they're something else! Countless stories, songs, and scattered memories, huh? The open road, landscapes changing like an IMAX movie, and if you're lucky, a radio station playing. My jam? Well, since you ask, I've got a mixed taste really, old school- metallica, ac/dc- to something more local like the Two Tons of Steel, y'know real south texas country rock, not the Nashville stuff ,catch 'em at Gruene Hall sometime, it's quite the drive but well worth it . Radio? I tune into KSYM, good old 90.1 FM, College radio but they have some of the best music, hands down. They do this "Third Coast Music Network" thing on Thursdays, looove it! Stay adventurous, amigo! Let the road take you where you need to go.

question_asked: I absolutely love the different cuisines you encounter when traveling. Specifically, I often find myself craving seafood right now. I had dungeness crab when I was visiting San Francisco and it was absolutely mouthwatering. Any type of seafood you fancy from your local area?
response: Oh, as a Beijinger here, I gotta tell ya, we're not famous for seafood like coastal cities, but have you heard about the Chinese mitten crab? It's a Shanghai delicacy, where I was born, and it's a must-try dish during the autumn season. The sweet, succulent meat and rich, creamy roe... ah, mouthwatering! But if you find yourself in Beijing, you gotta try Peking duck, pastries and hot pots. Nothing beats authentic local eats, huh? Still, there's that part of me that misses the freshness of seafood sometimes. Life of an inland architect, I guess! 🤷‍♀️🥢🦀

question_asked: Growing cacti and succulents has become my latest hobby, and I've found that the climate plays a substantial role in their wellbeing. I live in Arizona, so these drought-loving plants are right at home. It's been lovely spending time tending to them, witnessing their slow growth and sporadic blooming. You might not be into the spiky plants, so I was curious, which type of nature is more common in your town? Do you have lots of trees, or is it more urban?
response:
Ah, you're sitting amidst spiky pals, nice! Over here we've got the Tempelhofer field, converted from an old airport. It's not exactly full of succulents, but it's an urban green oasis of sorts, filled with kites, picnic lovers, wind skaters etc. 

And oh man, we have a lot of trees, lots of those leafy giants! Linden trees (or lime trees as some call 'em) are a big deal here. Whole city smells lovely when they bloom. When the wind blows... it's almost like some sort of natural perfume. 

And honestly, I love how a touch of nature weaves into the urban fabric here. Betwixt and between buildings, you spot a random tree or even roses wrapping around an iron fence. Makes the academic grind a bit softer, you know?

question_asked: I've recently started a new hobby, birdwatching. Living in California, I get to see some pretty cool birds, including the state bird, the California Quail. But my favourite spotting was when I got to see the white-tailed kite. It's amazing how they can hover in place with their body at a steep angle. Do you have any interesting birds where you live? Maybe even some that are unique to your area?
response: ah mate, i reckon we've got the best of both worlds here down under in Sydney. Lotsa urban birdlife, especially the iconic Aussie galahs and sulphur-crested cockatoos, they're everywhere! They can be cheeky buggers tho, especially those cockies, known to tear into wood and cause a fair bit of damage. But the real treat, mate, is the rainbow lorikeet. Their vibrant colours are just bloody captivating! Blood's worth bottling if you get to see 'em in your backyard! Not as exotic as your kites but it's all about the joys of home, right? Cheers from Straya, ya flaming galah! Enjoy your birdwatching!😄👍 🦜

question_asked: I had an interesting experience last year when I was traveling through Europe. It was remarkable how the daily life, food and even the weather differed from one country to the next. One of the highlights of my trip was Oktoberfest in Munich - the energy, the crowds, the music and of course, the beer. Speaking of beer, what's a popular local beer in your neck of the woods?
response: Oh man, mate, you're tapping right into my wheelhouse. We've got quite the array of craft beers. Ever heard of a little gem called La Fin Du Monde? Translates to 'end of the world', haha. It's from Unibroue, a real classic here. It's pretty strong, a tripel-style golden ale. If you glug down a pint of this, you'll sure feel like you're at the end of the world, ahah! It's got this taste that's just a notch above some of the other Canadian ales, the spices, you know? You should give it a go if you're ever this side of the great white north! Cheers!

question_asked: Gosh, this year's fall display in Japan has been truly amazing. The brilliant colors of the momiji (Japanese Maple) are an absolute treat to the eyes. I've seen the Maple leaves changing color from bright green to dark red in the neighborhood park and it's an absolute must-see sight. If you ever get a chance, what season would you say is the best to take in the natural beauty around your place?
response: Ah I say, if you fancy a blend of vitality and history, springtime is the key in our parts! the immaculate bloom of cherry blossoms around the colosseum... and lovely Magnolia trees near the Spanish steps. What a sight! As a history buff, I find the mix between natural beauty and ancient architecture absolutely breathtaking. and then, grabbing a gelato on the little cobblestone streets, it really reminds you how small our existence is compared to these eternal structures. You should witness it once, my friend, sublime! Top tip though, avoid the selfie stick vendors, they're relentless haha!

question_asked: Whenever I'm in Seattle, I always make a point of visiting the EMP Museum. I just love the blend of music, science fiction, and pop culture. Do you have any museums that celebrate pop culture where you're from?
response: Heard about a place called the Powerhouse museum mate, reckon it has some sorts of pop culture shows on displays, though i can't confirm as honestly, I've never been. My late missus was the museum goer in the family, but personally, I'm more into the digital world these days, spending heaps of my free time here online, you feel me?

question_asked: I can remember carrying out a road trip through Italy a few years back. Fondly called the "Italian Adventure." Started from the famous Milan, took a detour at Genoa, visit Pisa, and halted finally at Rome. Interestingly, it was an epic journey, trying different food and wines. I realized each region has a distinct food and wine taste. Have you ever noticed a difference in food tastes within your region or between your town and some nearby towns?
response:
Oh absolutely, mate. Even though India is often stereotyped with the label of curry, the thing on the ground is quite different. Our dishes are incredibly diverse and vary from region to region, sometimes even town to town. 

You see, I was born and brought up in Kolkata and the bangla fish curry there is without a doubt the best I've ever tasted. Spicy, flavourful with a punch of mustard. Now, I moved to Delhi for work, and although north Indian food is lip-smacking in its own right, the variety is completely different. More focus on wheat rather than rice. The paneer butter masala and the parathas here... man... 

And then there's the street food. The pani puri in Delhi is totally different from the puchka we have in Kolkata. Puchka beats out pani puri any day for me though haha! Also don't even get me started on the sweet dishes, the rosgulla in Kolkata, the jalebi in Delhi, they're all unique in their own ways. 

So yeah, just like your Italian Adventure, India also boasts of an extremely rich tapestry of culinary delights. It's a different adventure in every state! :)

question_asked: Travelling is indeed such a blast. Last year, I visited the city of Osaka, in Japan and tried Okonomiyaki for the first time, it's a delicious savoury pancake. Do you have any local dishes in your area that you could recommend? I love exploring new cuisine!
response: oh dude, if you liked Osaka's okonomiyaki then you'd definitely go nuts for monjayaki! it's like Tokyo's version of okonomiyaki with some difference but just as delicious. there's a spot in Tsukishima, where i often jog, that serves some killer monja. but just a heads up it looks a mess on teppan but believe me, it's mind-blowingly tasty! think i need to grab myself a plate tonight. haha

question_asked: One of my favourite neighbourhood activities is the morning market. It's just so vibrant and lively - people selling fresh veggies, butchers counter with fresh meat, fish mongers with the catch of the day. It's such an experience. They also have these flea markets where various local artisans come and sell their products. I once bought this beautifully engraved wooden watch from a local craftsman in San Francisco last time. The quality is top notch and the price was reasonable too! I just love how each city has its own character when it comes to local markets. Does your city have markets like that too? What unique local products have you found there?
response: Bacano, your neighborhood sounds super cool, man! We've got something similar here in Bogota. My barrio has a weekly market called "El Mercado de la Perseverancia." It's tiny compared to yours but full of character nonetheless; you can get a wide variety of fresh fruits, amazing Colombian coffee, local treats, artisanal crafts and more. It's always a blazing color splash and a complete sensory overload, I love it. Now, as a graphic designer, I'm always on the lookout for unique, handmade pieces, like graphic tees and cool print art. One of my prized possessions is this handmade poster from a local artist, it's got a beautifully drawn Botero-like pigeon on it, and I found it right there at the market. I guess that's my go-to place whenever I wanna add some local touch to my workspace at a good price. Definitely worth getting up early on a Sunday for. Trust me, just one freshly made arepa from there and you're hooked for life, haha.

question_asked: I love exploring food culture whenever I travel. Last summer, I stumbled upon an amazing culinary scene in Seoul, Korea. The street food was out of this world! However, what impressed me the most was Kimchi. Such a simple dish but so flavorful! Have you ever tried Kimchi, or any other particular dish that sets your locality apart?
response: oh si, si! you reminded me of the tapas scene right here in casa. nothing quite beats a good plate of gambas al ajillo washed down with a glass of sangria on a late summer evening ami derchesa, trust me! it's like a dance of garlic, shrimp, olive oil and chili flakes on your palate. and that's just the beginning, i mean, ever heard of cocido madrileño? oof, that's something else. your kimchi sounds exciting too, i might have to give that a try next time i'm trying out some foreign dishes online.

question_asked: I'm always curious about how time differences affect online gaming experiences. Friends and I often play multiplayer online games, but in different locations, it can be tough to all sync up - 9pm in LA usually means an early morning in Tokyo and a crazy late night in London. Do you experience any such inconveniences with time differences when you play online games? How do you manage it?
response:
Ah darn, tell me about it. As a 55-year-old financial manager, you would think online gaming differences won't bother me, eh? But I still like to game with my friends spread all around and time zones are a pain. Here in Montreal, we're in the Eastern Time Zone. Most of my gaming buddies are in similar zones, but I got a couple of them out west in Vancouver. Whenever we arrange to play something, I’m already snuggled up with my laptop ready to call it a night and they're still getting off work.  

But you know, I've learned to adapt over the years. What works for me is to find some common time that isn't too late for me (or too early for them), usually during the weekend afternoons. And it helps to play games that are not too time-sensitive, ones that you can casually play, put down and pick up again. Like card games and such - they're old school, But hey, if it ain’t broke.  

So, in the end, either I'm staying up later than I should, or they're gaming from work (shhh... don’t tell anyone!). English isn't my first language, but they say "you do what you gotta do," right? But ye, thats my experience, mostly reschedule and adapt. Hope that helps!

question_asked: During the summer, it's my personal pastime to attend festivals. Last year, I had an unforgettable time at the Notting Hill Carnival in London, such a variety of cultures and the music was just incredible! So, are there any festivals you've attended recently or do you have some recommendations?
response: Oh man, I'm a total fiesta head, can't lie. Two years back, I did this huge Lisboa crowd drawer, that Saint Anthony one in June, you know? Place was buzzing from every corner, sardines on the grill and all. Not usually my scene, but the vibe was something else. Definitely worth a looksee if you're in the neighbourhood during that time. The other one was this dope indie suppertime festival up north, where I grew up. Gets you stuffed with hearty food and your heart with good music. Ain't turned up recently though, blame that on my work, can't schedule a pee break even, forget a festival. Hoping things will ease up by June.

question_asked: I'm a bit of a winter nut myself, always have to make the most of it. Last time we were in Banff, my friends and I literally spent every second of daylight either skiing or snowboarding. What about you? How's the winter weather treating you this year? Have much snow where you live?
response: Ah man, snow...would be epic! But, alas, no can do in my parts. You get the odd frost here and there, but pretty mild in terms of winters. It's all about them fresh winds coming off the canals though, I guess. You get addicted to that crisp air in the morning commute, gives a cool wake up call. Kinda makes you just wanna pick up your bike and ride an extra mile on the icy paths for fun. You ever plan a trip this way, mate, bring a bike. Frost cycling here, prime Dutch winter experience, I tell ya!

question_asked: I've recently discovered rock climbing and have been loving it. My favorite one yet has been The Gunks in New York, just amazing views on top. Has the nature where you live got some nice climbing places too? Enjoying any outdoor activities there?
response: Of course! I've got an affinity for chasing sunsets. There's this place near the Bosphorus where I often drive to after work, and it has a magnificent view overlooking the water and the whole cityscape, especially at dusk. Climbing, though, haven't tackled it yet. My pals and I have been into street ball lately and there are some great spots hidden around the city for that. Next on my agenda? Kayaking on the Bosphorus or, you guessed it, maybe even bouldering on some Anatolian terrains, if time allows.

question_asked: From my experience, nothing compares to the thrill of fishing by the ocean. I once caught a striped bass while fishing by the Atlantic coast, it was tremendously exciting. Seafood markets around the coast are also a great way to get fresh produce. Have you ever gone deep-sea fishing? What kind of seafood is popular where you live? Or do you have access to more freshwater fish given your location?
response: aw mate, i gotta say as a Dutchie in Amsterdam, deep-sea fishing ain't no regular weekend activity for me. wish though, sounds like a great adventure! but yeah we do have our share of water. Canals n lakes n all, but ain't no sea monsters lurkin about haha. Seafood is another story. Haring (herring), heerlijk! and also have to mention Kibbling, deep fried pieces of cod, the real king of our straateten (street food), you gotta try it when you're round these parts, tastes completely lekker man! Plus you got yer traditional raw herring, slurped up with onions n all, a real dutch classic. Guess we lean more towards North Sea fish n mostly saltwater stuff, thanks to our lekker seaside location. Not much on the freshwater side that I know of, but hey, there might be somethin' lurking in those canals for all I know haha.

question_asked: I am a passionate coffee lover and Seattle, the birthplace of Starbucks, seemed like heaven to me. I tried to get a cup from every cafe there, but gave up soon, the number was simply overwhelming! How's the coffee culture in your town? Got any special places that roast their own beans or any special local coffee brands?
response: Ah, the love for coffee is universal! If you ever have the chance to visit my corner of the globe, check out the place called "Artisan Roast". They have their own blends and fair trade single origin coffee. Fair warning, their powerful aromas might get your heart beating like you've just spotted an unidentified celestial body, ha! And, definitely try their scones, when there's a cup of java in hand, the taste buds deserve a dance party too!

question_asked: I'm such a foodie at heart, and I recently took a trip to Argentina. The asados they have there are just amazing. Something about the combination of the wood fire and the quality of the meats just makes it something else, in my opinion. Do you have any staple foods or dishes where you're from that you think really set it apart from other places?
response: Oh man, absolutely... folks often associate feijoada with us, and while it's a banger - I kid you not - gotta tell ya about this regional favorite called acaçá. It's a damn work of art, man. A rice dumpling stuffed with dried shrimp, they dish it out around these parts like there's no tomorrow. Luring locals and tourists alike with that succulent scent wafting through the air from the beach stalls. It's like mesquite meets the sea, dude. Ah and with a spicy vatapá on the side. Mouth's watering here, I swear. A must-try if you're ever around in samba-land, for sure.
